author: yazan6546
body:
This pull request introduces significant changes to the project, including the addition of new modules for configuration handling, game mechanics, and player management, as well as restructuring the build system and graphical components. Below is a categorized summary of the most important changes:

### Build System Updates
* Added a new executable `main_baking` to the CMake configuration, including source files `src/main.c` and `src/utils/config.c`. Updated the `graphics` target to use `src/graphics/main.c` instead of `src/main.c`.
* Configured `main_baking` to include header files from the `include` directory.

### Configuration Management
* Introduced a `config.txt` file with detailed game settings, such as customer behavior, item categories, and operational parameters.
* Added `include/config.h` to define a `Config` struct and utility functions for loading, validating, and serializing configuration data.

### Game Mechanics
* Implemented core game logic in `src/game.c`, including initializing the game, simulating rounds, and checking game and round conditions. Added functionality to handle team efforts and determine winners.
* Defined a `Game` struct in `include/game.h` to manage game state, team performance, and round progression.

### Player and Team Management
* Added `include/player.h` to define `Player`, `Team`, and `State` types, along with player attributes and creation utilities.
* Created `include/player_utils.h` for player serialization, deserialization, and debugging utilities.
* Introduced `include/random.h` to generate random player attributes and initialize randomness.

### Graphics and Main Program
* Moved graphical functionality to `src/graphics/main.c`, which initializes a window and renders a simple texture and text.
* Simplified `src/main.c` to focus on loading configuration data and printing it, removing graphical logic.

body:
## Nová funkce: Bookmarky

Přidal jsem funkci bookmarků, která umožňuje uživatelům ukládat zajímavé zprávy pro pozdější použití.

### Příkazy
- `!bookmark [poznámka]` - Uloží zprávu, na kterou je odpovězeno
- `!bookmarks [stránka]` - Zobrazí seznam uložených bookmarků
- `!bookmark_delete <index>` - Smaže bookmark

Bookmarky se ukládají do souboru `data/bookmarks.json` a každý uživatel vidí jen své vlastní bookmarky. Potvrzení o uložení/smazání chodí do DM.

body:
**Description:**

This pull request introduces two new tools: `multi_web_search_exa` and `multi_crawling`.

**Key Changes:**

*   **New Tools:**
    *   Added `src/tools/multiWebSearch.ts`: Implements a tool for performing multiple web searches concurrently using Exa.
    *   Added `src/tools/multiCrawling.ts`: Implements a tool for crawling multiple URLs concurrently using Exa.
*   **Interface Updates:**
    *   Modified `src/types.ts`: Enhanced `ExaSearchRequest` and `SearchArgs` interfaces to include a `'never'` option for `livecrawl`. I noticed that when running multiple search queries simultaneously, it's helpful to turn off the livecrawl function so that the overall tool is more responsive.
*   **Tool Integration:**
    *   Updated `src/tools/index.ts` to export the new tools.
    *   Updated `src/index.ts` (for tool registration or usage).
*   **Improvements & Fixes:**
    *   Adjusted timeout settings and request handling in both new tools. Added rate limit information: If a user is using the multi-web search tool and they're sending more than five requests per second, they get a message to email hello@exa.ai to discuss an enterprise plan.
*   **Documentation:**
    *   Updated `README.md` to include information about the new tools.

**Feature**/**Bug fix**

## Acknowledgement

- [x] I acknowledge that I have read and understand the [Contributing](https://github.com/endless-sky/endless-sky/blob/master/docs/CONTRIBUTING.md) article.

## Summary
Since https://github.com/endless-sky/endless-sky/commit/f4f787b5c9b3717f9c983c75b437f6988805b620, the height of `TextArea`s can change after the initialization, which can cause unwanted offset if not handled properly, so we need to move the dialog resizing code from `Init` to `Draw`.

As a side effect, this also makes dialogs change their form (adding or removing scroll bars, or switching between the normal and double width) if the game window is resized.

body:
This pull request introduces several enhancements and new features, including updates to the build process, improvements in font and icon handling, and the addition of a new MAUI sample project with database integration. Below is a breakdown of the most significant changes:

### Build Process and Font Handling:
* Added a new `build.sh` script to initialize submodules, install dependencies, and build the Lucide font and icons.
* Updated `gen-codepoints.js` to copy the Lucide font file, adjust the CSS parsing regex, and modify the C# code generation logic for icon constants. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-4cb72becb876ca571f62010314f138c91f720cb3bb213ca3b06c9ad91ef29098L5-R18) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-4cb72becb876ca571f62010314f138c91f720cb3bb213ca3b06c9ad91ef29098L27-R36)

### Solution Structure:
* Updated `lucide-xaml.sln` to remove the `LucideIcons` project and add a new `LucideIcons.MAUI.Sample` project, along with its configuration.

### New MAUI Sample Project:
* Added `samples/LucideIcons.MAUI.Sample` with foundational files like `App.xaml`, `App.xaml.cs`, and `AppShell.xaml` to define the application structure and navigation. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2e16cbc522dc99729b2ec7bb4246c7f185231bcffe93585a181f905990aef8b7R1-R15) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-89e7cfc5f351ddae7f302adb602e10d7d785b18804e9b27b1e942647396e1a08R1-R15) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-944df2b2d8756d20e9909f1af0b7a40c7bf9d5bbe2093ea460f227526ab97fcdR1-R49)
* Implemented `AppShell.xaml.cs` with theme switching, snackbar, and toast notifications using CommunityToolkit.Maui.

### Database Integration:
* Added `CategoryRepository` for managing categories in a SQLite database, including CRUD operations and table initialization.
* Introduced `Constants.cs` to define database-related constants and paths.

### Serialization Enhancements:
* Added `JsonContext.cs` with source generation for JSON serialization of key data models.

# 🚀 싸피 15반 알고리즘 스터디 14주차 [김민진] ## 📌 문제 풀이 개요 - 이번 PR에서는 다음 5문제의 풀이를 포함합니다. - 각 문제에 대한 풀이 과정과 접근 방식을 설명합니다. --- ## ✅ 문제 해결 여부 - [x] **문제 1** - [x] **문제 2** - [x] **문제 3** - [x] **문제 4** - [x] **문제 5** --- ## 💡 풀이 방법 ### 문제 1: 상어중학교 **문제 난이도** 골드 2 **문제 유형** `구현` `시뮬레이션` `BFS` **접근 방식 및 풀이** 📍 `Group` — 우선순위 큐에 삽입     : 문제에 제시된 우선순위에 따라 `compareTo()` 오버라이딩     : `findBiggestBlock()`이 종료된 후 `poll()`한 값이 제거할 블록의 정보
📍 `findBiggestBlock()`     : `visited` — 게임 라운드마다의 방문, 일반 블록의 방문 여부만 저장     : `visitedRainbow` — 매 BFS마다의 방문, 무지개 블록의 방문 여부만 저장     → 무지개 블록은 중복 가능하기 때문 1. 방문하지 않은 일반 블록을 시작노드로 BFS 진행 2. 그룹에 넣을 수 있는 경우 `group` 리스트에 추가 3. 반복문 종료 후 `group`의 크기가 2 이상인 경우 `pq`에 삽입
📍 `removeBlock()` 1. `(블록 크기)^2`한 값을 `ans`에 더함 2. `group`을 탐색하며 해당 위치의 칸을 비움
📍 `gravitate()` 1. 각 열에 대해 가장 아래에서 시작 2. 빈 칸인 경우 건너뛰기 3. 검은 블록인 경우 `bottom` 업데이트 4. 그 외의 블록인 경우 `bottom`으로 이동 --- ### 문제 2: 게임 닉네임 **문제 난이도** 골드 3 **문제 유형** `트라이` `해시맵` **접근 방식 및 풀이** 1. `children == null`: 중복되는 prefix가 없다     → `null`이 나올때까지 `alias`를 더해주면 됨 2. 모든 글자를 확인했을 때 `cur.isEnd == true`라면 중복 닉네임이므로 숫자를 더해줌     → `HashMap`을 활용하여 닉네임의 갯수를 저장 3. 최종 완성된 `alias`는 `aliases`에 추가 --- ### 문제 3: 가장 긴 증가하는 부분 수열 5 **문제 난이도** 플래티넘 5 **문제 유형** `이분 탐색` `LIS` **접근 방식 및 풀이** 1. 각 숫자 당 증가하는 부분 수열의 가장 큰 인덱스(그냥 이분탐색 하면 나오는 값)를 저장하는 `idx` 배열 생성 2. 이분탐색하는 과정은 [LIS 2](https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/12015)와 동일 3. 이분탐색을 진행하며 `dp`에 값을 넣음     → 이 과정에서 `idx`배열의 값도 함께 업데이트     : 끝에 추가하는 경우 `dp` 배열의 길이     : 중간에 추가하는 경우 `target` 4. 모든 과정이 끝난 경우 `nums` 배열을 역순으로 확인하며 `ans`배열 업데이트     → `nums` 배열을 역순으로 확인하기 때문에 바로 출력하는 경우 배열이 반대로 나오기 때문     → 역순으로 확인해야 가장 긴 길이의 부분 수열을 확인할 수 있음 1. `(dp 배열의 길이 - 1)`인 부분부터 확인 2. `len--` 하면서 그 값을 부분 수열의 인덱스로 가지는 `num`들을 `ans`에 삽입 5. `ans` 출력 --- ### 문제 4: 경로 찾기 **문제 난이도** 실버 1 **문제 유형** `플로이드-워셜` **접근 방식 및 풀이** 플로이드 워셜 그대로 사용하면 됩니다 경로 유무만 필요하기 때문에 `boolean` 배열 사용해서 OR로 값 업데이트 했습니다 ```java graph[i][j] |= graph[i][k] && graph[k][j]; ``` --- ### 문제 5: 합 구하기 **문제 난이도** 실버 3 **문제 유형** `누적 합` **접근 방식 및 풀이** 단순 1차원 누적합 문제였습니다 ```java ... for (int i = 1; i <= N; i++) { int cur = Integer.parseInt(st.nextToken()); prefix[i] = prefix[i - 1] + cur; } ... sb.append(prefix[e] - prefix[s - 1]).append("\n"); ... ```

author: marcodimodica
body:
This pull request introduces a new `AudioManager` class to centralize and simplify audio management in the project, replacing the previous `SoundComponent` implementation. Key changes include the addition of `AudioManager` with comprehensive audio control functionality, the removal of `SoundComponent`, and updates to integrate `AudioManager` into the application.

### New Audio Management System

* **`AudioManager` Implementation**: Added a new `AudioManager` class with methods for initializing, playing, stopping, pausing, resuming, and scheduling audio playback. It also supports managing separate volumes for music and sound effects, and provides centralized control over all audio operations. (`AudioManager.cpp`, `AudioManager.h`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7b940534bcdb4684ad03e8366262db85c05c7b21281a3bb9404c21ecbf81b285R1-R293) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-1e3d183072c21832192ce6fb8ade33da7a17dda2c579ba60e81f9e2f5f51eefdR1-R67)
* **Project Integration**: Updated the Visual Studio project files to include `AudioManager` in the build process. (`MyAudioEngine.vcxproj`, `MyAudioEngine.vcxproj.filters`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3c62f658378615ba657ff8a4c6cdc182a9944e138cf602428ad6dba2a461bf39R137-R142) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-59223410456d8e4731be5538f32c916f7465eb28339d8096451c2f0dde3d6059R24-R26) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-59223410456d8e4731be5538f32c916f7465eb28339d8096451c2f0dde3d6059R35-R37)

### Removal of `SoundComponent`

* **Deprecated `SoundComponent`**: The `SoundComponent` class and its associated functionality have been commented out, effectively deprecating it in favor of the new `AudioManager`. (`SoundComponent.cpp`, `SoundComponent.h`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-64327f5f4278f8765812440f0e0d169e9196b9171b5ddc8a6dcb451f55fd1e52L1-R120) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7529c4a8ef342035f0dcadd0d368ed228bc1374975d392d288e0703ee1b49ab6L1-R43)
* **Removed Usage**: Eliminated references to `SoundComponent` in the input handling logic and other parts of the application. (`Input.cpp`)

### Application Updates

* **Integration of `AudioManager`**: Replaced the `AudioEngine` instance in the `App` class with calls to `AudioManager` for audio updates, ensuring the new system is used throughout the application. (`App.cpp`, `App.h`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-8f554abe5ca729ea7be5729f51aa46f082f1a378ca4bf2f8891ad38ec5d25eb3R14) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-8f554abe5ca729ea7be5729f51aa46f082f1a378ca4bf2f8891ad38ec5d25eb3L41-L43) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-8f554abe5ca729ea7be5729f51aa46f082f1a378ca4bf2f8891ad38ec5d25eb3R127-R128) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-9196ecf41035c265f63a004fa29afedcf5a1d0d0d98ec972b850c10ac8b5953fL74-L75)
* **Miscellaneous Cleanup**: Removed unused or commented-out code in several files to streamline the codebase. (`Root.cpp`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-1db1763febc7c7116c847b8c659b89f29d21eb20a64313fda084251c529ae69aL49) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-1db1763febc7c7116c847b8c659b89f29d21eb20a64313fda084251c529ae69aL217) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-1db1763febc7c7116c847b8c659b89f29d21eb20a64313fda084251c529ae69aL254-R255)

This overhaul simplifies audio management, consolidates functionality into a single class, and improves maintainability by removing the now-redundant `SoundComponent`.

author: ckerr
body:
#### Description of Change

Part 1 in a series to enable/fix tests that didn't run due to #46807. 

This step fixes three issues with the `visibleOnAllWorkspaces` tests:

- The tests were enabled on Windows, even though Windows doesn't support this feature
- The tests were skipped on Linux, even though Linux supports this feature
- Due to nested `it()` statements, the tests were not run on any platform (which is why they didn't fail on Windows :smile_cat:)

This PR fixes these by running the tests on Linux and macOS.

All reviews welcomed. CC @nikwen who reviewed the original PR.

Added data rate and logging changes.  The data rate change in particular fixed a big problem on the update where the floor just showed garbage.  This was due to the newer version of RaspbianOS seems to have a different default SPI speed which overran the ATMega168 that drives the differential pair to the floor, experiencing ~80% loss of data. Also began some structure changes that are better suited to simple commits to main.

author: amcandio
body:
### Summary

This PR optimizes the `girvan_newman` community detection algorithm in NetworkX.

The Girvan-Newman method is known to be computationally expensive, and users have reported performance concerns:
- [StackOverflow: Why is the Girvan-Newman algorithm in NetworkX so slow?](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/62951320/why-is-the-girvan-newman-algorithm-in-networkx-so-slow)
- [Issue #7992: Improve runtime of `girvan_newman()` function](https://github.com/networkx/networkx/issues/7992)

In [#7992](https://github.com/networkx/networkx/issues/7992), two optimization opportunities were identified:
1. **Cache the number of edges** and update it incrementally after every edge removal.
2. **Operate on one graph per connected component** to allow better caching of edge betweenness centrality.

This PR implements the **first optimization**: the number of edges is now cached and updated incrementally.  
The **second optimization** is not implemented here because it would require a deeper refactoring: the current method accepts a `most_valuable_edge` function that operates on the **full graph**, making per-component caching of betweenness centrality non-trivial.

### Performance

Benchmarks comparing current and optimized versions (averaged over 100 runs):

| Graph Type                   | Current Time/Call (s) | Optimized Time/Call (s) | Speedup |
|-------------------------------|-----------------------|-------------------------|---------|
| Complete Graph (n=10)         | 0.016050               | 0.015241                 | 1.05×   |
| Complete Graph (n=20)         | 0.170338               | 0.149063                 | 1.14×   |
| G(n=50, p=0.1)                | 1.068046               | 1.092481                 | 0.98×   |
| G(n=50, p=0.2)                | 4.944922               | 4.612656                 | 1.07×   |


Performance improvements are clear for larger or denser graphs, and small changes for easier graphs are inconclusive and likely due to normal benchmark variability.
Speedups range between ~0–14% depending on the graph structure.

### Benchmarking Code

The following code was used to measure runtimes:

```python
import timeit

setup = "import networkx as nx"

benchmarks = [
    ("Complete Graph (n=10)", "list(nx.community.girvan_newman(nx.complete_graph(10)))", 1000),
    ("Complete Graph (n=20)", "list(nx.community.girvan_newman(nx.complete_graph(20)))", 100),
    ("G(n=50, p=0.1)", "list(nx.community.girvan_newman(nx.fast_gnp_random_graph(50, p=0.2, seed=1)))", 100),
    ("G(n=50, p=0.2)", "list(nx.community.girvan_newman(nx.fast_gnp_random_graph(50, p=0.5, seed=1)))", 100),
]

for label, stmt, c in benchmarks:
    duration = timeit.timeit(stmt, setup=setup, number=c)
    per_call = duration / c
    print(f"{label:<30} | Total time: {duration:.4f}s | Time per call: {per_call:.6f}s")

author: kmk3
body:
Treat them like `/dev/tpm[0-9]*` devices.

It seems that `/dev/tpm[0-9]*` allows direct access to the TPM device
while `/dev/tpmrm[0-9]*` mediates access through a "resource manager"
inside of the kernel (for example, to facilitate concurrent access).
Alternatively, it looks like the resource management can be done in
userspace through tpm2-abrmd, the "TPM2 Access Broker & Resource
Management Daemon", which also supports older kernels (Linux 3.x vs
4.12) [1] [2] [3].

udev rules from tpm2-tss 4.1.3[4]:

    # tpm devices can only be accessed by the tss user but the tss
    # group members can access tpmrm devices
    KERNEL=="tpm[0-9]*", TAG+="systemd", MODE="0660", OWNER="tss"
    KERNEL=="tpmrm[0-9]*", TAG+="systemd", MODE="0660", GROUP="tss"

This is a follow-up to #6718.

Misc: This was noticed on #6700.

Relates to #6390.

[1] https://github.com/tpm2-software/tpm2-abrmd
[2] https://github.com/tpm2-software/tpm2-abrmd/issues/830
[3] https://github.com/tpm2-software/tpm2-tss-engine/issues/149
[4] https://github.com/tpm2-software/tpm2-tss/blob/4.1.3/dist/tpm-udev.rules

author: kszafran
body:
Description
-------------

This PR adds support for generating [gomock](https://github.com/uber-go/mock) mocks. It's a follow-up to a [PR](https://github.com/uber-go/mock/issues/245) I created directly to gomock, trying to add a batch mode in order to reduce generation time.

Using mockery, I got an even better improvement in generation time. Calling mockgen on 78 packages in my project sequentially:
```
       61.13 real       270.97 user       132.04 sys
```
Running mockery to generate them all at once:
```
        2.23 real         2.76 user         7.13 sys
```
which is almost 30x reduction in real time (40x in CPU time).

This PR also includes a few small improvements:
- calling `SignatureNoName()` will now avoid wrapping single return arg in parentheses — `(string)` -> `string`
- types are now not repeated in arg lists and return arg lists if not necessary — `(a int, b int, c int)` -> `(a, b, c int)`
- a few small features added to support the new template: `.SrcPkgName`, `.SrcPkgPath`, `.Interfaces.NameList`, `list` and `append` functions

I tried to keep the template file close in structure to the original `mockgen` code, so that it's easy to update in the future to reflect changes in `mockgen`.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] This change requires a documentation update

Version of Go used when building/testing:
---------------------------------------------

- [ ] 1.22
- [ ] 1.23
- [x] 1.24

How Has This Been Tested?
---------------------------

I regenerated mocks using mockery in my private project. The output is pretty faithful to the code generated by `mockgen`.
The differences I noticed are:
- Different file header. I tried to keep the style close to the existing mockery templates. Generated by `mockgen`:
  ```
  // Code generated by MockGen. DO NOT EDIT.
  // Source: github.com/owner/repo/path/to/pkg (interfaces: Interface,Another)
  //
  // Generated by this command:
  //
  //	mockgen -typed -destination=mockpkg/mocks.gen.go -package=mockpkg . Interface,Another
  //
  ```
  Generated by `mockery`:
  ```
  // Code generated by mockery; DO NOT EDIT.
  // github.com/vektra/mockery
  // template: gomock
  // source: github.com/owner/repo/path/to/pkg (interfaces: Interface, Another)
  ```
- Imports aren't aliased if not necessary (`mockgen` _always_ uses aliases like `gomock "go.uber.org/mock/gomock"`).
- `mockery` always suggests some nice arg names in `Do`, `Return`, `DoAndReturn` (these functions take the return args of the mocked method), while `mockgen` uses `arg0`, `arg1`, ...
- `mockery` keeps arg names in function types (`f func(projectIDs []string)`), while `mockgen` drops them (`f func([]string)`)

Checklist
-----------

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines of this project
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my code
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

body:
## About The Pull Request
Adds three Runic weapons craftable by Hearthkins, two being reskins of shaft miners crushers, one being a sidegrade of the base crusher. As well as a xenoarcheology find used for said craft.
Runic Greataxe : Functionally the same as a base crusher. Sprite is an edited version of a sprite from https://github.com/GeneralPantsuIsBadAtCoding/Azure-Peak (I tried finding the actual spriter but roguetown codebase isn't too documented, feel free to contact me if you know and i'll add them).
Runic Spear : Functionally the same as the spear crusher. Sprite was made by me.
Runic Greatsword : Functionally the same as the base crusher with one exception. It cannot fire a marking projectile, in exchange, the right click action marks all targets (that could be marked by a normal crusher) in melee but doesn't break rocks. The sprite is reused from the moonlight greatsword.
Dormant fragment of the Stjarndrakkr : Found through xenoarcheology, or in the abandoned temple ruin. Hearthkins can use a chisel on them to reawaken them, the reawakened fragment can then be crafted using the crafting menu with a piece of leather, a piece of wood and a smithed tool head into the weapon corresponding with the tool head used. The recipe also requires the use of a smithing hammer. The sprite is reused from the cult whetstone.
## How This Contributes To The Nova Sector Roleplay Experience
Hearthkins characters usually place a great deal of roleplay importance into the "hunt" as a concept, yet they can neither obtain nor uses trophies, this lets them do so while also encouraging trading with both the station and Interdyne. As both roles will be more likely to actually obtain the fragments the Hearthkins would need to forge those weapons. Seeing as the boulder machines produces a lot of xenoarchology rocks.

author: ahmedmuqawi
body:
## Changes Made
- Separated pagination parameters for appointments and doctor performance tables
- Introduced `doctorPage` URL parameter for doctor performance pagination
- Kept `page` parameter exclusively for appointments pagination
- Updated query keys in useReports hook to reflect the new pagination structure

## Problem Solved
Previously, changing the pagination in the appointments table would trigger unnecessary API calls to the doctor performance endpoint due to shared pagination parameters. This was causing performance issues and redundant server requests.

## Solution
- DoctorsTab now uses `doctorPage` instead of `page` for pagination
- useReports hook has been updated to handle separate pagination parameters
- Each table now maintains independent pagination state
- API calls are now properly isolated between the two features

## Technical Details
- Modified `DoctorsTab.jsx` to use `doctorPage` parameter
- Updated `useReports.js` to track both `page` and `doctorPage` separately
- Adjusted query keys in React Query to prevent unnecessary refetching
- Maintained backward compatibility with existing pagination logic

## Testing
Please verify:
- Appointments table pagination works independently
- Doctor performance table pagination works independently
- No cross-triggering of API calls when changing pages in either table
- URL parameters update correctly for both tables

## Additional Notes
This change improves the application's performance and reduces unnecessary server load by preventing duplicate API calls.

author: h0tch0colat3
body:
## What does the pull request do?
When adorner layer is detached then attached to visual tree, the adorner element is added to the layer's children before the element is attached to the visual tree. This results in `adorner.CompositionVisual` being null, and logic that would otherwise be run is skipped. Adorners in this scenario are then drawn in the incorrect position. This PR adds logic to handle that case and draw adorners correctly.


## What is the current behavior?
Visual layer managers which appear in scenarios where they may be detached and then attached to the visual tree will draw adorners incorrectly.


## What is the updated/expected behavior with this PR?
Adorners are drawn correctly when contained in visual layer managers that may be detached from the visual tree


## How was the solution implemented (if it's not obvious)?
Modify the `ChildrenCollectionChanged` function of `AdornerLayer.cs` to add logic which:

1. Checks if the adorner is already attached to visual tree. If so, call `UpdateAdornedElement` as before
2. Otherwise, add a listener for when the adorner is attached to the visual tree, then call `UpdateAdornedElement`
3. Add a case for `NotifyCollectionChangedAction.Remove` which removes the handler added in step 2


## Checklist
- [ ] Added unit tests (if possible)?

## Breaking changes
N/A

Fixes #18734 (and also fixes the related exception mentioned in that issue)

… events

This change fixes the issue where the last character of key bindings was being passed through to the opened window/action. Now we ensure that:
- Group bindings use key press events (on press)
- Leaf/terminal bindings use key release events (on release)

This way, the key press is properly consumed by the action before it can be passed to the newly opened window.

By treating group bindings as on press, we ensure that perfomance gains mentioned in #3 are retained

body:
Refactor CompanyPromoDetailView from a generic APIView to DRF’s RetrieveUpdateAPIView in order to leverage built-in retrieve/update behavior and simplify the implementation.

Key changes:
- Use `RetrieveUpdateAPIView` as the base class to get object lookup, serialization, validation and response handling for free
- Remove manual `get()` and `patch()` methods
- Add `business.permissions.IsPromoOwner` to `permission_classes` for declarative authorization
- Define `queryset = Promo.objects.with_related().only(...).for_company()` on the view to centralize and optimize data access
- Implement `with_related()` and `for_company(user)` on the Promo queryset/manager for efficient prefetching and filtering
- Drop unused imports and old helper code

This change reduces boilerplate, improves consistency with DRF idioms, and makes permission checks and queryset logic easier to maintain.

author: vvk93
body:
This PR introduces a Python script (userboard_pipeline.py) that orchestrates an end-to-end simulation of a user feedback board using LLMs and LangChain.

Core Functionality:

Data Loading: Loads clustered user review data (from cluster_outputs/clusters_data.json).
Feature Ideation: Uses an LLM (ideate_features) to brainstorm potential product features based on negative sentiment clusters.
Persona Generation: Creates distinct user personas (generate_personas) from cluster data using an LLM.
Board Simulation: Simulates a multi-round discussion (simulate_board) using a ConversationChain for each persona to gather feedback on the proposed features. Personas maintain conversational memory and respond based on their profiles.
Summarization: Generates a concise summary (summarise_meeting) of the discussion highlights and outcomes using an LLM.
Reporting: Compiles all inputs, generated content, the discussion transcript, and the summary into a final Markdown report (write_report).
Orchestration: Uses LangGraph (build_pipeline) to manage the flow between these stages.

How it Works:
The script defines configuration in a Config dataclass, sets up logging, and uses modular functions orchestrated by a LangGraph pipeline. Each stage passes its output to the next, culminating in a comprehensive report. It relies on environment variables for the OpenAI API key (OPENAI_API_KEY in a .env file).

Results:
The primary output is the multiagent_outputs/board_session_report.md file, containing the selected clusters, proposed features, generated personas, full discussion transcript, and the final summary.

Here, add a new complimentary pair for `HookWorkBegin`: `HookWorkEnd`,
which runs after workers finish, taking in an error result. `HookWorkEnd`
hooks may or may not modify the error result, choosing to suppress an
error on pass it along the stack unchanged.

This is driven by trying to add a new `nilerror` contrib package [1]
that helps detect nil error-compliant structs that return non-nil error
interfaces, which is a common footgun in Go [2].

## Motivation
resolves #332 
This pull request introduces a production deployment preview workflow, similar to Vercel's preview system.
When a PR is opened and/or a new commit is pushed on a PR, the workflow will build the docker image and then run the rain solver bot docker image in production environment for a full round (number of rounds are configurable through repository variables, default is 1).

The preview link directs to the exact HyperDX instance associated with the current commit hash.

#### 119ab85f69fdcd30bf83c12c957ddcec0f2781c8 
[JSC][GreedyRegAlloc] buildLiveRanges can track interval end rather than interval
https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=292104
rdar://150113046

Reviewed by Yijia Huang and Yusuke Suzuki.

Rather than keeping a set of live Intervals, we can instead just
track the ends of the intervals. It's a bit cheaper to do this
bookkeeping since merging Points into an Interval requires checking
both the Interval's begin and end. But since buildLiveRanges()
processes points in decreasing order, we only need to track the
end of live intervals. Also this avoids the need to iterate the
liveAtHead for each block.

This improves readability since the bookkeeping abstraction is now in
terms of use/def rather than intervals, which is a bit more idiomatic.
Also, it removes a special case for clobbers that was required when
processing them out-of-order w.r.t. other use/defs.

author: dinocosta
body:
This Pull Request attempts to fix an issue where using `d}` in vim mode would not delete all characters in case there's no blank lines at the end of the buffer.

When calculating the end point for this motion, if there's no blank lines at the end of the buffer, Zed was calculating it to be the last character in the last line. However, if there's a newline at the end of the buffer, it calculates the end point to be the point at the right of the last character.

Here's an example, for the following buffer contents:

```
Hello!
Hello!
```

If the `d}` command is run at `(0, 0)`, the end point will be set to `(1, 5)`. However, fi the same command is run for this buffer instead:

```
Hello!
Hello!

```

The end point will be set to `(1, 6)`, there's a 1 unit difference in the column, which leads to all characters actually being deleted.

Closes #29393 

Release Notes:

- Fixed deleting to the end of paragraph when there's no blank lines

author: codersmiti
body:
This PR introduces a regression test suite for the i.eb.evapfr module in GRASS GIS. The tests verify that the module correctly computes the evaporative fraction (EF) based on given net radiation, soil heat flux, and sensible heat flux inputs.
The test suite ensures correct statistical behavior under various conditions and validates the robustness of energy balance calculations.

**Key Updates in This PR**

**Functionality:**

- Validates core EF calculations for standard inputs by checking that evaporative fraction outputs produce expected univariate statistics (mean, min, max, stddev).
- Tests handling of the -m flag by verifying that soil moisture outputs are generated correctly when requested, and match expected statistical behavior.
- Confirms that increasing sensible heat flux results in a lower evaporative fraction.
- Confirms that increasing net radiation results in a higher evaporative fraction.
- Ensures that linearly scaling all input energy fluxes (net radiation, soil heat, sensible heat) does not alter the computed evaporative fraction, maintaining energy ratio consistency.

**Test Case Additions:**

- Basic Calculation Test: Validates evaporative fraction output statistics for standard input maps.
- Soil Moisture Output Test (-m flag):Ensures that soil moisture is correctly computed and matches expected statistical properties.
- Sensitivity to Sensible Heat: Verifies that increasing sensible heat decreases evaporative fraction output.
- Sensitivity to Net Radiation: Verifies that increasing net radiation increases evaporative fraction output.
- Scaling Invariance Test: Ensures that doubling all energy inputs does not affect the evaporative fraction outcome.

Description: Integrate computer vision capabilities to allow the voice banking system to process physical documents via mobile camera
Developed a module that uses OCR and document analysis to extract information from ID cards, bank statements, or payment slips when photographed
When a user says "Transfer money using this payment slip":

- The system recognises this as a document-related command
- Camera activates with guidelines for positioning a payment slip
- System captures the document and extracts payment information (amount, payee, reference)
- Information is presented to the user with a confirmation request
- The user can confirm or cancel the transaction by voice
- System completes the transaction and provides feedback

test.iypnb shows the work of document_processor.py.

body: ### Summary of Changes 1. **Added `schema.sql`** - Created two separate schemas: one for Keycloak and the other for the remaining application. 2. **Dynamic Realm, Role, Frontend, and Backend Client Creation** - Implemented logic to dynamically create realms, roles, frontend, and backend clients in Keycloak. 3. **Validation Dependency Added** - Introduced a validation dependency for improved data validation. 4. **Email Validation for User Creation** - Added required email validation in **User** entity to ensure that Keycloak can successfully create a user. 5. **User Management in `UserService`** - Implemented functionality to create and delete users in Keycloak. Users can now be added or removed via API. ### Notes - This update enhances the integration with Keycloak, enabling seamless user management and role/realm configuration. - The validation ensures that the user data provided is correct before being processed. ## Summary by CodeRabbit - **New Features** - Integrated Keycloak for user authentication and management, including automated realm, client, and role setup on application startup. - Added database schema initialization scripts for gym and Keycloak schemas with appropriate privileges. - Added global exception handling for validation errors with clear error messages. - Enhanced user management to synchronize user creation, update, and deletion with Keycloak. - Enforced email format validation and booking relationship on user entities. - Added support for cascading deletion of user bookings. - **Improvements** - Upgraded Keycloak and related dependencies for improved security and compatibility. - Enhanced Docker Compose setup for PostgreSQL and Keycloak initialization, networking, and debugging. - Updated application configuration for schema management and frontend integration. - Improved validation of user input in controller endpoints. - **Bug Fixes** - Ensured that deleting a user also deletes all associated bookings automatically. - **Tests** - Added comprehensive unit tests for Keycloak integration, user service, and Keycloak initialization logic. - Introduced test configurations to mock Keycloak interactions for isolated testing. - **Chores** - Updated `.gitignore` to exclude documentation and log files. - Refined build and migration scripts for better maintainability and initialization control.

author: johnnasseh
body:
Currently has support for returning walking and driving time based on the user's address through OpenRouteService. Ideally, we could request the user's location through the frontend and use that, but it might be too late to implement it. It doesn't give bus transit data. Google requires billing information to use their Google Distance Matrix API. All of the other bus transit APIs are cumbersome or not worth using. I applied for access to the NJ Transit API, and hopefully I'll get it by Wednesday. 

Honestly, this entire feature feels pointless. You can easily pull this information in seconds through Google/Apple maps, and it'll be 100% accurate. The latitude and longitude that Ticketmaster returns for Events isn't exactly the most accurate. author: manuelfragata
body:
Addresses multiple errors encountered during tolerancing tests (test_add_operand, test_apply_compensators, test_add_perturbation) when running with both NumPy and PyTorch backends (with autograd enabled).

The primary issues involved incorrect handling of PyTorch tensors requiring gradients when interfacing with SciPy optimizers and incorrect attribute access in tests.

Specific changes include:

- Refactor optiland.backend.utils.to_numpy:
    - Ensure correct handling of lists containing scalar types (Python or NumPy numbers) and potentially gradient-requiring tensors.
    - Modified list processing to recursively convert elements (detaching tensors via 	orch_to_numpy) and construct a 1D NumPy array from the resulting scalar values.
    - This fixes ValueError: 'x0' must only have one dimension. and the RuntimeError: Can't call numpy() on Tensor that requires grad. when converting lists passed to SciPy.

- Refactor optiland.optimization.optimization.OptimizerGeneric (and subclasses):
    - Convert the initial guess list x0 (potentially containing backend tensors/arrays) to a 1D NumPy array using the fixed 	o_numpy before passing it to scipy.optimize.minimize and other SciPy optimizers (e.g., in LeastSquares, DualAnnealing). This fixes the RuntimeError originating from SciPy's input processing.
    - Modify the objective function _fun to:
        1. Accept the NumPy array x from SciPy.
        2. Convert it back to a backend-native tensor using  e.array for internal Optiland calculations (allowing autograd flow within the objective function). 3. Convert the final scalar result 
ss back to a standard float using  loat(to_numpy(rss)) before returning to SciPy.
    - Update the undo method to use stored backend-native values.

- Fix 	ests.test_tolerancing.test_add_perturbation:
    - Correct attribute access for surface radius to use optic.surface_group.surfaces[...].geometry.radius. This fixes AttributeError related to accessing optic.surfaces or surface.radius directly.

Note: The specific change of adding _fun_residuals for the LeastSquares optimizer was not implemented per discussion. The LeastSquares class still passes the scalar-returning _fun to scipy.optimize.least_squares, which may lead to suboptimal or incorrect behavior for that specific SciPy function.

author: j-bahr
body:
Add "unpadded" support to Base64 encoder/decoder

Motivation:

This patch aims to improve the flexibility of the base64 encoder to allow it to be used more broadly as a general purpose base64 encoder by supporting output with no padding. While RFC 4648 suggests that base64 is always padded, Base64 URL does not require padding in all circumstances, especially when length is known ahead of time. The implementation in Netty assumes the length is always the size of the buffer. In this case the decoder can produce correct output regardless of whether padding is added for either Base64 or Base64 URL encoding.

When the encoder receives an unpadded Base64 URL string today it is possible that one or two bytes are omitted from the resulting buffer. By detecting if these bytes were not processed we can infer the necessary padding and produce the full length decoded source text. Similarly on the encoding side we can omit the padding if the user elects to do so.

Modifications:

Decode:
The `ByteProcessor` on the decode loop processes 4 bytes at a time, calling `decode4to3` using a byte[] buffer of size 4. When the `ByteProcessor` completes and there is no padding, the final call to `decode4to3` will not have been made. We can infer based on the index into the 4 byte buffer how much padding is necessary and we can make the final call to `decode4to3` with appropriate padding added.

Encode:
If no padding is necessary, we can simply omit the padding bytes at the end of our processing rounds instead of appending them.

Result:

The base64 encoder will support encoding and decoding Base64 without padding. The decoder will handle both modes gracefully, and the encoder will by default add padding, as is suggested by the RFC, but will allow the user to elect not to in the event they want padding omitted.
